targetWords.definition: An aim is a goal someone wants to make happen.
targetWords.example: My aim is to become a helicopter pilot.

targetWords.definition: To attach is to put two things together.
targetWords.example: I attached the socks to the clothesline to dry.

targetWords.definition: To bet is to risk money on the result of a game or a business.
targetWords.example: How much will you bet that your horse will win?

targetWords.definition: A carriage is a vehicle pulled by a horse.
targetWords.example: ■We took a carriage ride in the park.

targetWords.definition: If something is classic, it is typical.
targetWords.example: The athlete made a classic mistake-he started running too soon.

targetWords.definition: To commute is to travel a long distance to get to work.
targetWords.example: I usually commute to work on the train.

targetWords.definition: To confirm is to make sure something is correct.
targetWords.example: Winning the game confirmed that James was a good player.

targetWords.definition: He criticized his wife forspending too much money.
To differ is to not be the same as another person or thing.
targetWords.example: I differ from my brother: he is short, while I am tall.

targetWords.definition: An expense is the money that people spend on something.
targetWords.example: She wrote down all the expenses for her trip.

targetWords.definition: If something is formal, it is done in an official way.
targetWords.example: It was a formal dinner, so we wore our best clothes.

targetWords.definition: Height is how tall someone or something is.
To invent something is to create something that never existed before.
targetWords.example: ■My grandfather has invented some interesting things.

targetWords.definition: If someone is junior in their job, they do not have a lot of power.
targetWords.example: When she started at the company, she was only a junior manager.

targetWords.definition: Labor is the act of doing or making something.
targetWords.example: Building the house took a lot of labor.

targetWords.definition: A mechanic is someone who fixes vehicles or machines.
targetWords.example: We took the car to the mechanic to be fixed.

targetWords.definition: If something is prime, it is the most important one.
targetWords.example: Dirty air is a prime cause of illness.

targetWords.definition: t
targetWords.example: He shifted to the other side of the table to eat his breakfast.

targetWords.definition: A signal is a sound or action that tells someone to do something.
targetWords.example: The coach blew his whistle as a signal to begin the game.

targetWords.definition: When people are sincere, they tell the truth. He sounded sincere when he apologized to me. ^05

story.title: Henry Ford's Famous Car
story.passage:
My name is Henry Ford, and I invented a car called the Model T. I used to

watch carriages on the streets. They fascinated me. Then I got a job as a junior

mechanic. My father criticized me. He wanted me to run the farm. But I did not

shift my plans.

Then I worked for the Detroit Auto Company. But I wanted to make cars using

less labor. That way, there would be fewer expenses. I started the Ford Motor

Company in 1903. At first, the company did not do well. But many people were

betting on my success. I also had a sincere aim to make a car that anybody

could buy.

Then, in 1908,1introduced the Model-T in a formal ceremony. It confirmed

that I was right: it was possible to build a car my way!

The Model T differed from other vehicles. Workers could attach different parts

for cars or trucks. This saved time. One Model T could be put together in 93

minutes. All of them had the same classic design. They were all the same size

and height. The prime reason for doing this was to save money.

Over 19 years, I sold over 15 million

Model Ts. This sent a signal

to other companies.

People would buy cars

to commute to work

if the price was low

enough.
